svg.title: Reflex v3 neural architecture
svg.desc: End-to-end architecture for an order-invariant open-option classifier. A frozen Nemotron encoder produces query and candidate embeddings. A shared Deep Sets candidate network scores every option, symmetric rank statistics feed a small NONE neural network, and a K plus one softmax chooses a candidate or NONE OF THESE.
svg.text: Reflex v3 · Order-invariant open-option neural selector
One frozen text encoder + one shared candidate network + one rank-aware NONE network → a variable-size K + 1 decision
Solid arrows are inference. The candidate branch is evaluated independently for every offered option with shared weights.
candidate logits z₁…zₖ bypass the NONE net
B. Candidate scorer — a literal neural-network view
This branch runs K times. Weight sharing makes candidate scores move with the candidates when their order changes.
rᵢ = concat(s, cᵢ, s ⊙ cᵢ, |s − cᵢ|) ∈ ℝ⁸¹⁹²
mean ignores order and supports any K
• φ and ρ are the same networks for every option.
• mean(h₁…hₖ) is unchanged by a shuffle.
Therefore shuffling options only shuffles z₁…zₖ.
Training signals for each candidate score
Ranking CE: the present gold should outrank other options.
Pair-match BCE: zᵢ has a stable absolute match meaning.
That stable scale is what the NONE network reads later.
A tiny neural net learns “is the correct answer available?”
No raw query embedding · no label identity · no candidate position
Return argmax: one offered option or NONE_OF_THESE.
Key separation: the candidate network learns which option matches.
The NONE network learns whether any offered option is good enough.
